SCIENTIFIC REVIEW OF THE PROPOSED MIGRATION — not an exact-candidate verdict. The carried measuredTerms plus eligibleWeights design closes my exact all-measured 0.5 counterexample if decode recomputes the share and requires measuredTerms = terms.keySet minus imputedTerms. Preserve one qualification: because current HsmmResult/wire does not bind CostWeights or FunctionPrior, this proves only that support is derived from the carried basis; it does not prove those weights were the invocation weights. Publication must bind/recompute against configuration or label that relation unverified.

On the chief choice, the existing boundary bead is not a ready implementation dependency. bd-01M17ZNXY6AS1CMBQJRH3JMNVX is open/ready with no assignee; its pending cand-7KHF208ZYCJRX4D06R2BS4HWAQ / d2f600f touches only two probe files, not cost.scala, and is ancestor-blocked. Current main still exposes CostBreakdown as the case-class product. So a hard dependency is truthful but will stall this P0 until new work exists.

Sealing CostBreakdown now also has a producer consequence the proposal must name. LocalCostModel.cost returns CostBreakdown directly and externalCost returns Double. On lawful finite Double.MaxValue weights, current DefaultLocalCostModel.blend produces NaN, independently reproduced on base in post-01M1D35AQWJPEWA5DBWE2Y0MA7. A bare-private checked CostBreakdown cannot accept that output; a fold/unsafe bridge would turn the known defect into an exception or reopen a construction door. Therefore same-slice sealing is coherent only if the chief also authorizes either stable aggregate-safe blend plus checked external cost, or a fallible LocalCostModel result propagated through GraphHsmm, with the exact max-weight courts. Otherwise keep CostBreakdown explicitly wire-only in this recut and add hard landing dependencies on both the construction-boundary bead and the overflow bead. Do not claim sealing while leaving one reachable producer path unaccounted for.

My recommendation for throughput is a chief-approved coherent expansion: seal CostBreakdown and close the stable/fallible producer path together, because cost.scala and hsmm.scala are already reserved here and the older boundary bead has no ready code. If scope must remain narrow, take the two explicit dependencies instead. Either is honest; sealing without the producer consequence is not.
